verified_facts.text: The hotel is on the corner of Ayala and Makati Avenues in Makati City, Metro Manila.
verified_facts.excerpt: Corner of Ayala and Makati Avenues, 1226 Makati City, Metro Manila, Republic of the Philippines

verified_facts.text: The hotel is 9 km from Ninoy Aquino International Airport.
verified_facts.excerpt: 9 km from Ninoy Aquino International Airport / 6 km from Manila Domestic Airport

verified_facts.text: The Peninsula Manila celebrates its 50th anniversary in 2026.
verified_facts.excerpt: In 2026, it celebrates its 50th anniversary with Condé Nast Traveler Gold List recognition and MICHELIN-selected awards for Old Manila and Spices.

verified_facts.text: The hotel was designed by Filipino architect Gabriel Formoso as a double-winged Brutalist building.
verified_facts.excerpt: a double-winged Brutalist beauty designed by Filipino architect Gabriel Formoso

verified_facts.text: The hotel was built ahead of the 1976 International Monetary Fund conference.
verified_facts.excerpt: financial hub of Makati, ahead of the 1976 International Monetary Fund conference

verified_facts.text: The triple-height Lobby is crowned with a sculpture of bronze, copper and steel that resembles a bursting sun.
verified_facts.excerpt: They all fill the soaring sun-filled atrium crowned with a sculpture of bronze, copper, and steel that resembles a bursting sun, the beating heart of this hotel.

verified_facts.text: Old Manila serves French fine dining in an Art Deco setting.
verified_facts.excerpt: Indulge in an unforgettable French fine dining experience at Old Manila—where stunning Art Deco design

verified_facts.text: Old Manila's private dining room, the Magsaysay Room, is named after President Ramon Magsaysay, whose oil portrait hangs there.
verified_facts.excerpt: is named after the Philippines’ most beloved President, Ramon Magsaysay, whose oil portrait commands the room.

verified_facts.text: In 2026, Old Manila and Spices are MICHELIN-selected.

verified_facts.text: Escolta serves an international buffet.

verified_facts.text: The Peninsula Halo-halo Harana is the hotel's version of the Filipino dessert halo-halo, served in a giant glass.

verified_facts.text: Rooms have been refreshed with contemporary Filipino design, natural textures and views across Makati.
verified_facts.excerpt: Newly refreshed rooms express contemporary Filipino design through natural textures, intuitive technology and views across Makati.

verified_facts.text: The Gallery Club Lounge overlooks The Lobby and the Sunburst sculpture, surrounded by works by Philippine masters, and serves breakfast, afternoon tea and evening cocktails.
verified_facts.excerpt: surrounded by works by Philippine masters. The exclusive access offers breakfast, afternoon tea, and evening cocktails with a curated selection of spirits.

verified_facts.text: The Peninsula Spa offers traditional Filipino treatments such as the Hilot Massage with Ventosa.

verified_facts.text: The spa has a minimum age of 18.

verified_facts.text: The spa area also has saunas and steam rooms.

verified_facts.text: The hotel has a bespoke jeepney painted in Peninsula Brewster Green.

verified_facts.text: A program for young guests includes local games, scavenger hunts and exercise classes.

verified_facts.text: From the hotel, guests can walk to Legazpi Village, Salcedo Village, Poblacion and the Greenbelt Mall complex.
